text:
[ITST.5.5.2] A scenario **must** take six steps, in this order: stand up the
probe, build the engine, load the rules, drive it, check the observable, tear
it down. The probe's state **must** live on the scenario function's stack, and
step 5 **must** assert on what the probe recorded, not on what the engine
currently contains.

That order is what makes the isolation claim structural rather than a
discipline ([ITST.5.5.1]). Probe state lives on the **stack** of the scenario
function, so it cannot survive into the next scenario whether or not anyone
remembers to reset it, and the engine is built after it and freed before the
function returns. Nothing about a scenario outlives its own frame.

Step 5 is the one that decides whether the test is worth anything: the
assertion reads what the probe **recorded**, not what the engine currently
contains. A scenario that reaches past its probe has started testing the
implementation instead of the claim.

The function's name is its citation ([ITST.5.3]).
